transcript.text: Every so often when I use the hob the electrics in the house go off. Not every time, maybe once a week. It's an induction hob, Hisense I think.

An induction hob tripping your house electrics is almost certainly an earth-leakage fault. Because it's intermittent, it could be a failing power module inside the hob, moisture tracking under the glass (if spills have occurred), or a loose mains connection at the fused spur. Please stop using the hob if you smell burning plastic or see scorch marks; in that case, isolate it immediately and call an engineer. And are there any other appliances on the same circuit that might be contributing?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
Kettle is on sometimes at the same time. Also there was a faint electrical smell once after it tripped, but no burning that I could see. I've had a couple of boil-overs on it recently too.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning smell or smoke can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The combination of tripping electrics, recent boil-overs, and that faint electrical smell points strongly to an internal earth-leakage fault. In induction hobs, this is typically caused by moisture from spills tracking into the power module or control electronics, damaging insulation. Because there was a burning smell, this is a safety hazard: please stop using the hob immediately and isolate it at the fused spur (the switch box on the wall) to prevent further damage or fire risk. This fault cannot be safely fixed as an owner; you need a qualified electrician or appliance engineer to inspect the internal wiring and replace the damaged module. Please do not attempt to reset it repeatedly.
